column1: # Every data set the recipes read that a publisher serves, declared once: the set (its directory under $LAPLACE_DATA), how it
# is fetched, its origin, and where under the set it lands. data.sh fetch pulls each from its origin at the latest, at the
# machine's own network speed; Laplace-Engine/recipes/*/source names the roots the recipes read them from.
#   mirror   the publisher's directory, as it serves it (wget -r): into . keeps its path under the set; into a directory
#   file     one file: into is the path under the set it lands at (a directory when it ends with /: the origin's own name)
#   listing  a GitHub contents listing (api.github.com/repos/O/R/contents/PATH): every file of it, into a directory
#   release  the latest GitHub release (api.github.com/repos/O/R/releases/latest): the asset matching into's pattern;
#            {edition} in the set's name is the asset's name after the pattern's literal prefix, before its extension
#   extract  an archive the set already holds (origin: its path under the set), opened into a directory under the set
#   git      a repository into a directory under the set: at the commit after @ in into (pinned: every host the same), or at the
#            latest of its default branch when there is none
#   archive  an archive from the publisher, kept under the set's .archive and opened into the set (into: a directory under the
#            set, or the archive's file name when the URL does not carry one, e.g. a repository's bitstream)
# Unicode 17.0.0, pinned: the version ICU 78 and tier 0 are built from (laplace.env). The recipes and the Engine read it at
# Public/UCD/latest, the name the publisher's rolling directory has; what is there is 17.0.0, not whatever is latest today.
# FrameNet 1.7 as NLTK redistributes it (CC BY 3.0 per NLTK's index; Berkeley FrameNet's own release is on request); VerbAtlas 1.1.0 as
# its publisher serves it (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: the download page asks the licence be accepted; LICENSES.txt is in the archive)
# Tatoeba's weekly exports: the publisher keeps only the current week, so these are the latest by nature; the record (fingerprint.sh
# inputs) says which week a host holds. users_sentences is not among the exports it publishes today.
# Wiktextract's raw dump of the English Wiktionary (kaikki.org): one current file, replaced in place by the publisher (2.8 GB); the
# record says which dump a host holds. The recipe matches raw-wiktextract-data*.
# Universal Dependencies 2.18, pinned: the release LINDAT/CLARIAH holds (hdl.handle.net/11234/1-6149), the treebanks and the documentation
